title: Profiteroles
subtitle: Choux pastry puffs with cream and warm chocolate sauce
excerpt: Light, hollow choux pastry balls, split and filled with whipped cream, piled high and drizzled with a warm dark chocolate sauce. A classic French dessert.

recipe.sourceNotes: Profiteroles are small cream-filled choux pastry puffs, one of the most widely known forms of the French choux pastry tradition. Choux paste (pâte à choux) is unique among pastry types in that it is cooked twice: first on the hob, where the flour is beaten into boiling water and butter to form a thick paste, and then in the oven, where the steam from the water in the paste causes the pastry to puff up dramatically and hollow out as it sets. The name profiterole originally referred to a small profit or bonus given to servants in a household; by the nineteenth century it had come to refer specifically to the cream-filled pastry. The chocolate sauce is an integral part of the dish in the French tradition: the contrast between cold cream and warm chocolate is deliberate.

recipeTools.notes: Two baking trays lined with baking parchment. A piping bag is helpful but a teaspoon works fine.
A medium saucepan for the choux paste and a small saucepan for the chocolate sauce.

content.text: The choux paste must be beaten hard after each addition of egg: the paste will initially look as though it has split but will come back together with vigorous beating. Add the eggs gradually and stop when the paste falls from the spoon in a slow, reluctant V shape. Too much egg makes the paste too loose to hold its shape; too little makes the pastry dense. Pierce the base of each bun with a skewer as soon as they come out of the oven to let the steam escape, which prevents them collapsing.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Put 200 ml water, the butter, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a rolling boil. Remove from the heat and tip in all the flour at once. Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a smooth ball that leaves the sides of the pan clean. Return to low heat and cook for 1 minute, stirring, to dry the paste slightly.

Beat in the eggs one at a time, beating hard between each addition until the paste is smooth and glossy. Stop when the paste falls from the spoon in a slow V. Spoon or pipe 24 walnut-sized balls onto lined baking trays, spacing them well apart. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped. Pierce the base of each immediately with a skewer. Cool on a wire rack.

Whip the cream to soft peaks. Split the cooled buns and fill each with whipped cream. For the sauce: heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chopped chocolate, add the butter and sugar, and stir until smooth. Pile the profiteroles on a serving dish and drizzle with the warm sauce. Serve immediately.
